Title: Prevent duplicate events and harden GPS capture
Problem / Request: The July 15 field session confirmed duplicate current-Pulse offer rows at 10:45, 11:13, 11:42, 12:13, 12:44, and 13:49, plus two one-minute zero-mile Trip Log artifacts near 12:44. The Rebuild captured five accepted rides but reused the same cached coordinates from 10:18 through 12:10 and produced no trip/drop-off rows. Implement one-event-per-action handling, client event IDs, server-side idempotency, a short duplicate lock, and a resilient GPS helper that reports fresh, cached, fallback, or unavailable status instead of silently reusing stale coordinates. Keep this task focused on event integrity and location quality; trip lifecycle is PULSE-013.
Acceptance Criteria: One iPhone tap creates exactly one event; repeated delivery of the same client event ID is ignored; rapid duplicate taps are rejected safely; GPS first requests a fresh position, then may use a recent cached position only within a defined age limit, otherwise records unavailable; each event stores GPS status, age, accuracy, and capture source; ping and trip pickup/drop-off controls use the same helper; the July 15 fixture reproduces no duplicate rows and flags stale GPS; normal and test modes pass; no merge or deployment occurs automatically.
Branch / Build: Field reconciliation completed; run next through Builder token
Last Error: Do not expand this patch into routing, background tracking, or the full state machine.
